Hurried lull rules for handover notes
This section sets out the standard that applies

Companion Animal Travel Desk Standard for Pet Travel Handover

This section guides the handling of travel notes, booking reviews, and passenger support for animals traveling with Aurelia Skyways. The Companion Animal Travel Desk must respond with calm, clear language and must keep each record accurate, complete, and ready for the next colleague who may continue the file. Every handover note should state the current status of the booking, any customer concern already addressed, and any action still pending, so the service remains steady and kind.

When a traveler raises a concern, staff should acknowledge it promptly, confirm the next step in plain language, and record any special instruction that affects the journey. If the case involves a small dog, <<FACT F068>> Staff must place that inserted sentence within the running note without adding any extra wording around it, so the record remains exact and usable. For rabbits, the same care applies, and <<FACT F064>> The inserted sentence must appear as a full sentence in the note, with no added explanation or commentary.

Each handover must avoid unclear language, rushed shorthand, and assumptions about what another colleague will understand. Where a crate, carrier, or travel arrangement needs review, the note should say what has been checked and what remains to be confirmed, using direct words that can be followed at once. The desk should never leave a customer facing repeated explanations when the detail is already on file, and it should preserve a respectful tone even when the case is urgent.

Staff may mention the traveler by name when needed for clarity, but only when the name is already part of the booking record and relevant to the note. The guiding principle is shared responsibility, so every colleague should write as though another person must continue the journey without delay or confusion. If any instruction is uncertain, consult the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor for immediate guidance.

For any unresolved case, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at once.
